results: 1. Complete neuro-ophthalmic examination, including ocular alignment and motility in all directions, convergence, saccades, smooth pursuit, pupils, eyelids, and fundus examination
cranial nerve examination: limited right eye adduction failing to cross midline, with left abducting nystagmus on left gaze; otherwise normal
fundoscopy: normal
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
smooth pursuit and saccades: normal
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): limited adduction of the RIGHT eye that fails to cross the midline, with abducting nystagmus of the left eye on left gaze - mimics an INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
vertical gaze and convergence: normal
pupil size and light reaction: equal and reactive
ptosis / lid position: none
2. Alternate cover test and prism measurement of the ocular deviation at distance and near
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
3. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain and brainstem with gadolinium, including thin-section images through the medial longitudinal fasciculi
MRI brain with gadolinium: normal brainstem; subtle medial orbital wall fracture with medial rectus involvement
4. Magnetic resonance angiography of the intracranial circulation
CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): normal / non-contributory
5. Serum acetylcholine-receptor antibodies and muscle-specific kinase antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative - excludes ocular myasthenia, the commonest cause of pseudo-INO
6. Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine
TSH / free T4: normal
7. Serum glucose or HbA1c, blood pressure measurement, and lipid profile
blood glucose and HbA1c: normal
glucose / HbA1c: normal
lipids and vascular risk assessment: normal
8. Lumbar puncture for cerebrospinal-fluid cell count, protein, oligoclonal bands, and IgG index if brain MRI shows an inflammatory or demyelinating lesion
lumbar puncture / CSF: normal cells and protein; no oligoclonal bands
CSF cell count and differential: normal
CSF protein: normal
CSF oligoclonal bands and IgG index: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Right medial rectus mechanical restriction/entrapment from a subtle medial orbital wall fracture, causing a traumatic pseudo-internuclear ophthalmoplegia

Alternatives:
1. Isolated right medial rectus palsy from an orbital branch of the oculomotor nerve injury
2. Orbital myositis or early thyroid eye disease affecting the right medial rectus
3. Ocular myasthenia gravis with pseudo-internuclear ophthalmoplegia
